draft.title: Why people work
card: Work is effort that people put into making goods or providing services. Most people work to earn income, which is money received. Income pays for needs such as food and housing, and for wants.
Many people also work for satisfaction. They enjoy the job, or feel proud when they do it well.

Work can give a sense of purpose, such as helping others or doing something that matters. It can also build skills, make friendships with workmates and shape how people see themselves, such as "I am a nurse".
People weigh these reasons differently. One person may work mainly for income. Another may take a lower-paid job because it gives more purpose or satisfaction.
draft.remember: People work for income, and also for satisfaction, purpose, skills, friendships and identity.

a.q: Leila works at a local animal shelter. Which reason for working is NOT about income?
opts: She feels her work has a purpose in helping animals
She needs money to pay for her phone plan
She wants to save for a holiday
She uses her pay to buy her lunch
a.why: Feeling that the work has a purpose is a reason for working that does not depend on money. The other three are all about using pay to buy things, so they are about income.
a.clue: Which reason does not involve spending money?

b.q: Tom is offered two jobs. One pays more but is lonely and has no new learning. The other pays less but has a friendly team and teaches him new skills. He takes the lower-paid job. What does this show?
opts: People can work for reasons other than income
People work only for friendships and skills
Income is not a reason that people work
Lower pay always makes a job better
b.why: Tom gave up some income for friendships and skills, so people can have reasons beyond income. It does not mean income does not matter, and it does not mean other reasons always win. People weigh the reasons differently.
b.clue: Tom still earns money, but it was not his only reason.

a.best: She feels her work has a purpose in helping animals

b.best: People can work for reasons other than income

b.q: Tom is offered two jobs. One pays more but is lonely and has no new learning. The other pays less but has a friendly team and teaches him new skills. He takes the lower-paid job. What does this show about Tom?
opts: He valued friendships and skills above the extra pay
He valued the extra pay above friendships and skills
He chose the job that gave him the most income
He took the job mainly to help others in need
b.why: Tom gave up some income to get friendships and new skills, so he valued those above the extra pay. Saying he valued the pay more reverses his choice, since he turned down the higher-paid job. Nothing in the scenario says he took the job to help others.
b.clue: Look at what Tom gave up and what he gained.
